turns.customer: Ember 0°C down bag or the Drift -5°C synthetic: which is warmer, and which is lighter?
turns.reply: On warmth (temperature rating): the Drift -5C is the warmer bag - it's rated to -5C, while the Ember 0C is rated to 0C. So the Drift handles colder nights. But one caveat: down (Ember) keeps its insulation better than synthetic (Drift) when kept dry, while synthetic holds warmth better if it gets damp - the temperature number only covers dry conditions. So on a dry trip, the -5C Drift is the warmer spec. If you expect moisture or condensation, the picture is closer, but the rating still favors the Drift. On weight: the Ember 0C is much lighter at 850 g, versus the Drift -5C at 1700 g - more than half the weight. So the Ember wins on lightness; the Drift -5C wins on the cold-rating. Quick summary: Ember 0C Down - 850 g, 0C rating, $259.00 (4.7 stars). Drift -5C Synthetic - 1700 g, -5C rating, $139.00 (4.3 stars). Both in stock. Let me know your typical trip temps and whether you're carrying over long distances - that usually settles it.
